not_judged.TMR-ADDR-WIDTH-RANGE: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) always sets ADDR_WIDTH, to 4 and to 8 (lines 75, 648 and 649), so the default is never used and widths 5 to 7 are never built; a block whose default is 5, or that aliases offsets from 0x10 up only at width 6, passes it.
not_judged.TMR-PORTS-ONLY: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) connects the ports by name (lines 75 to 83), and Icarus Verilog builds an instance that leaves a port of the block unconnected, so a block with an extra port passes it. The widths of the named ports are checked (lines 461 to 480, TMR-PORTS).
not_judged.TMR-LOAD-ZERO-PERIODIC: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) runs periodic counts only with LOAD 7 (lines 379 to 399), LOAD 30 (lines 450 to 452), LOAD 8 (lines 589 to 603) and LOAD 300 (lines 605 to 618), and LOAD 0 only in one-shot mode (line 356), so a periodic count with LOAD 0 is never run.
not_judged.TMR-COUNT-READ: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) never checks the value of COUNT while a count runs: it compares COUNT with a value only at reset, after a one-shot count ends, after a COUNT write and after a stop (lines 314, 298, 331, 403 to 404, 409, 457, 529, 575, 577, 579 and 587). The two reads of a running COUNT (lines 428 and 430) check only that RDATA and RRESP hold still while RVALID waits and that the response is OKAY. COUNT's value during a count is judged only through the edge the count ends on (TMR-COUNT, TMR-COUNT-LENGTH) and the value a stop leaves (TMR-STOP-EDGE).
not_judged.TMR-CTRL-WINS: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) never lands a CTRL write on the edge a count ends: its only writes timed to a count end are the STATUS clears at lines 395 to 398 and 441 to 444, and the stops of its periodic runs are checked to land before the next count end (lines 602 and 617). No mutant breaks this rule.
not_judged.TMR-IRQ-EDGE: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) reads irq after a write only once write_ok returns, after the response handshake two edges after the write takes effect (lines 301, 368, 370, 547, 549 and 551), so an irq that follows an IE write or a STATUS clear one or two edges late is not caught. The rise after a count end is timed, under TMR-COUNT-LENGTH.
not_judged.TMR-READY: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) sees readiness only through the handshakes of the transfers it offers, one at a time: each write and each read runs to its response before the next starts (lines 111 to 212), and it never reads AWREADY, WREADY or ARREADY otherwise. So the 'only if' halves (no acceptance while a response waits or while the same half is held) and readiness across the two directions are never exercised; a block that drops AWREADY while RVALID is high is not caught. Writes completing in either order are judged under TMR-ORDER.
not_judged.TMR-READ-VALUE: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) never checks a value read on an edge on which that register changes: COUNT only while it holds still (see TMR-COUNT-READ; the reads of a running COUNT at lines 428 and 430 check no value), CTRL and STATUS only on edges on which no count ends, LOAD never during a write. So a read that returns the value after the accepting edge is not caught.
not_judged.TMR-RESET-EDGE: The reference testbench (evals/flow/axil_timer/axil_timer_tb.v) drives aresetn low only at power up, where BVALID, RVALID and the held halves start unknown rather than high, and in the middle of a count with no transfer in progress (lines 274 to 282, 308 to 310 and 450 to 454), changing it only between rising edges. So it never sees a pending response or a held half write dropped by reset, and does not tell a synchronous reset from an asynchronous one. The manager rule is an assumption on the testbench, which keeps it.
not_judged.TMR-CLEAN: Lint and synthesis are the RTL stage's own before-review checks, not held-out checks.
not_judged.TMR-TB-ALL: The must-fail check holds the flow's testbench to passing on the reference RTL and failing the four committed timer mutants (cited under mutants), and to nothing more: a testbench that leaves any other requirement of sections 2 to 6 unchecked, or times only some counts to the edge, still passes it.
